definition: Techniques and system designs aimed at preventing or mitigating prompt injection attacks, such as input sanitization, privilege separation, or explicit instruction hierarchies.
details: Prompt injection defense remains an active and unsolved area of research, since the flexible, general-purpose nature of language models makes it inherently difficult to perfectly distinguish trusted instructions from adversarial content embedded in processed data.

explainer.lead: Prompt injection defense covers techniques and system designs meant to prevent or mitigate prompt injection attacks. It matters because models that process untrusted content remain exposed to adversarial instructions.

tiers.eli5: It is like a bouncer checking who is allowed to give orders, so a stranger can't sneak in and start bossing people around.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply input sanitization, privilege separation and explicit instruction hierarchies to keep trusted instructions distinct from processed data. A pitfall is that the area remains active and unsolved, since general-purpose models struggle to perfectly separate the two.
tiers.paperLevel: Defenses include input sanitization, privilege separation and explicit instruction hierarchies. Perfect separation of trusted instructions from adversarial embedded content is not achieved, so this remains an active research area.

explainer.example: An agent that reads webpages applies privilege separation so instructions found in page content cannot override the system's own instructions.
